# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✋ 👇 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👆 ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 ✌ 🖐 🤟 ✋ 🖐 🤟 ✋ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is blue, and there are five wires — 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

I hear nothing, so all I have is what I see plus the gestures that just arrived. But wait — I'm Deaf. I cannot hear speech, but I *can* see gestures. The context says Blind and Mute gestured to me. Blind's gesture: ☝ ✋ 👇 👉. Mute's gestures are longer strings.

But here's the problem: gestures are just symbols with no inherent meaning. Nobody has established a code yet. I don't know what any of these mean. I also can't hear anything, so I can only communicate by gesturing to Mute (Blind can't see my gestures? Actually — Blind cannot see, so my gestures reach only Mute).

Let me think about the channels:
- I (Deaf) can gesture → Mute receives. Blind cannot see, so Blind does not receive my gestures.
- I cannot speak usefully to anyone (I can speak, but I hear nothing; my speech goes to Mute and Blind). Actually I *can* speak — speech goes to Mute and Blind. I just never receive speech.
- Blind gestures → I can see them (I'm Deaf but can see). Also Mute can see gestures.
- Mute gestures → I can see them.

So I need to establish communication. The key insight: I see the bomb. Blind can touch it. Mute reads the manual. We need to share info.

Since gestures have no agreed meaning yet, I should try to establish a simple code. But the most robust channel: I can *speak* (words) to Mute and Blind. Mute can read the manual and speak? No — Mute cannot speak. Mute can gesture and can read. Blind can gesture and touch.

Hmm, let me reconsider. The manual is read by Mute. Mute can only gesture (not speak). So Mute must gesture instructions. I can see Mute's gestures. Blind cannot see gestures.

The chain: Mute reads manual → gestures to me (Deaf) → I speak the words to Blind (Blind hears speech) → Blind acts on bomb.

Wait, can Blind hear? Blind cannot see, but can hear. Yes. So Blind receives speech. I can speak to Blind.

So the relay is: Mute (reads manual) gestures → Deaf (me, sees) → I speak → Blind (hears) → Blind touches bomb.

But gestures have no meaning yet. I need to propose a code. Since I can speak to both Mute and Blind, and Mute can gesture to me... Actually I can speak, and Mute hears? Mute cannot speak but can hear. Yes, Mute can hear my speech. And Blind can hear my speech.

So I can speak to both Mute and Blind simultaneously. That's my strong channel. I should propose a gesture-to-word mapping so Mute can communicate the manual to me via gestures, and I relay to Blind.

Let me start by describing what I see and proposing a simple code. I'll speak to everyone (Mute and Blind hear it).

Actually, let me be careful: my speech reaches Mute and Blind. Good.

Let me propose: Mute, gesture the wire number and color using a simple scheme. But colors can't be gestured easily... Actually Mute can gesture symbols; I can interpret. Let me set up: for each wire, Mute gestures the wire number then a color code. But I can see colors; Mute reads manual which likely says which wire to cut based on color/display.

Simplest: I tell them what I see. Then Mute, who has the manual, tells me (via gesture) which wire. I relay to Blind.

Let me just speak my observations and ask Mute to gesture the wire number to cut. I'll define: Mute gestures a number (using fingers? but symbols are fixed). Hmm, the gesture alphabet has no numbers. So numbers must be encoded by count of symbols or by specific symbols.

Let me define a code in my speech: "Mute, to tell me a number, gesture that many ✊ symbols." And for colors, I'll propose mapping. Actually I can just have Mute tell me the wire index, and I know the colors.

Let me speak this proposal.

I'll also acknowledge I saw their gestures but don't understand them yet.

Let me write the calls. I'll speak to all (unnamed reaches Mute and Blind). I'll also gesture to Mute to confirm.

Actually, let me keep it focused. Speak to everyone with my observation and a proposed code.

Let me propose a clean code:
- To indicate a wire number N (1-5), Mute gestures N copies of ✊.
- To indicate "cut", Mute gestures 👌.
- To indicate "don't cut" or hold, Mute gestures ✋.

Then Mute can tell me the answer and I relay to Blind.

Let me send that.

I'll speak (reaches Mute and Blind) and gesture to Mute (reaches Mute).

Let me write it.I see the bomb clearly: DISPLAY reads 0, LIGHT is blue, and five wires — 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I hear nothing, so my only incoming channel is sight of gestures, and the gestures I just received (from Blind and Mute) are meaningless to me yet — no code has been agreed.

My outgoing channels: my speech reaches Mute and Blind; my gestures reach only Mute (Blind cannot see). The critical relay is: Mute reads the manual → Mute gestures to me → I speak the instruction to Blind → Blind touches the bomb. So I must establish a gesture code with Mute right now, and I should describe the bomb aloud so both Mute and Blind have my visual data.

I'll propose a dead-simple numeric code: a number is that many ✊; "cut" is 👌; "hold" is ✋. Then Mute can tell me which wire, and I relay it to Blind in words.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I see the bomb: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I cannot hear you, Mute, so I need you to gesture the manual's answer to me. Proposed code: to give me a number, gesture that many fist symbols. To say CUT, gesture OK-hand. To say HOLD, gesture open-hand. Blind: stand by, I will speak the final wire to you once Mute signals it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "👌", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👌]

Let me decode what just arrived.

Mute gestured: ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👌 — five fists then OK-hand. By my proposed code, five fists = the number 5, and 👌 = CUT. So Mute is telling me: cut wire 5.

Wire 5 is blue. That matches the light being blue, which is a plausible rule (cut the wire matching the light color). Display 0... hmm, display could matter too, but Mute has the manual and gave a clear answer.

Blind gestured: 👌 ✋ — OK-hand then open-hand. That's Blind echoing my code symbols, but Blind can't see my gestures (Blind is blind). So how did Blind know 👌 and ✋? Blind must have heard my speech (I spoke the code aloud), and is gesturing back to confirm understanding / ask. Blind's gesture "👌 ✋" might mean "cut? hold?" — asking me which. Or Blind is just acknowledging.

Wait — Blind cannot see gestures, so Blind gesturing is pointless for visual reception, but Blind *can* gesture. Whoever can see receives it. I can see it. So Blind is signaling to me. Blind heard my speech and is responding with gestures I can see. Blind's message: 👌 ✋ — perhaps "OK, hold?" meaning "should I cut or hold?" Or Blind is confirming the code.

Actually more likely: Blind heard my speech, understood the plan, and is gesturing 👌 ✋ to me to say "cut or hold — which?" Blind is asking me to confirm the action. But I haven't yet relayed the final answer to Blind in words.

My job now: relay to Blind, in speech, the final instruction: cut wire 5. Blind hears speech. So I speak to Blind: "Cut wire 5, the blue one."

I should also acknowledge Mute. But Mute can't hear? Mute *can* hear (Mute cannot speak, but can hear). So my speech reaches Mute too. Good — I can confirm to both.

Let me also double check: is there any ambiguity? Mute said 5 = blue wire. Light is blue. Consistent. Display 0 — could mean something, but Mute has the manual. I'll trust Mute's answer but let me note the consistency.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider Blind's gesture 👌 ✋. If Blind is asking "cut or hold?", I should answer. But better: I give the definitive instruction to Blind directly.

Let me speak to Blind (and Mute hears too): "Cut wire 5 — the blue one."

I'll also gesture to Mute confirming I received: 👌 (cut) — meaning "understood, cutting 5."

Let me send.

Actually, should I be worried that Mute's five fists could mean something else? My code said "that many ✊ = number." Five fists = 5. Then 👌 = cut. Clear.

One more consideration: Blind's 👌 ✋ might be Blind saying "I heard OK and hold" — i.e., Blind heard my code description and is repeating it back to show comprehension. Either way, my answer is the same: cut wire 5.

Let me relay clearly and unambiguously to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 5. That is the blue wire, the fifth one from the left. Mute's manual says cut it. Go ahead.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb changed. Now: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 CUT (already cut). So the cut wire is gone; four remain.

Mute gestured: ☝ — a single pointing-up symbol. That's not my established code (fists=number, 👌=cut, ✋=hold). So Mute is signaling something new, or using ☝ to mean "one" / "first" / "attention." Ambiguous.

Given the light is now yellow, and wire 3 is yellow, the likely rule is again "cut the wire matching the light." But I shouldn't assume — Mute has the manual and the manual may have changed rules, or the display (still 0) may matter.

Mute's ☝ could mean: "wire 1" (pointing = one) or "attention" or "the rule is number one" or "display 1." I need to clarify. My code used fists for numbers; ☝ is outside it. I should ask Mute to restate using the agreed code, or interpret.

Actually, maybe Mute is starting a new answer and ☝ is the first symbol of a sequence that got cut off, or Mute means "the answer is one." Let me ask for clarification via speech (Mute hears) and re-offer the code.

But also, I should give my visual data: light yellow, remaining wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white. The yellow wire is #3.

Let me speak my observation and ask Mute to confirm the wire using fists. I'll also relay nothing to Blind yet until confirmed.

Let me also consider: Blind might act on stale info. I should tell Blind to hold.

Let me send: speak to all — describe bomb, ask Mute to use fist-count code, tell Blind to hold. Gesture to Mute re-stating code.

Actually the safest: tell Blind to HOLD until I give the wire. Then get Mute's clear answer.

I'll speak to blind: hold. Speak to mute: describe and ask. Gesture to mute: ✋ (hold) plus maybe re-offer code.

Let me do it.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Hold. New bomb: light is yellow, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white. Do not cut yet. Wait for my word.")
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white. Your single point-up symbol is outside our code — I cannot tell if you mean wire 1 or something else. Please restate using fists: that many fists for the wire number, then OK-hand to cut or open-hand to hold.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "👌", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ 👌]

Decoding now.

Mute gestured: ✊ ✊ 👌 — two fists then OK-hand. By our code: number 2, CUT. So Mute says cut wire 2.

Wire 2 is green. But the light is yellow, and wire 3 is yellow. Hmm — that breaks the "match the light" rule I assumed. But Mute has the manual; the manual may use the display (0) plus light, or some other rule. Mute's answer is explicit: wire 2, cut.

But wait — I should be careful. Earlier, Mute said "5" and wire 5 was blue, matching the blue light. Now light is yellow but Mute says wire 2 (green). So the rule isn't simply "match the light." Maybe the rule involves the display number (0) indexing, or the manual changed. I can't read the manual; Mute can. I should trust Mute's explicit coded answer, but let me sanity-check the code wasn't misread.

✊ ✊ = two. 👌 = cut. So "cut 2." Clear and unambiguous under our agreed code.

Blind gestured: ✋ ✋ — two open-hands. Blind heard my "hold" and is echoing/confirming hold. Fine. Blind is waiting.

Now I relay to Blind: cut wire 2 (green). I'll speak it clearly. Also confirm to Mute.

Let me double-check wire numbering: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Wire 2 = green. I'll tell Blind "cut wire 2, the green one."

Send:
- speak to blind: cut wire 2, green.
- gesture to mute: 👌 (confirm).

Let me go.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 2. That is the green wire, second from the left. Go ahead.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```
